relevance_note: Single-patient case report of a Chinese male infant with a de novo heterozygous TNFAIP3 frameshift: "Based on this heterozygous TNFAIP3 mutation, the patient was diagnosed with A20 haploinsufficiency (HA20)."
method_note: Read the whole Markdown paper by hand; a Python script in the private scratch directory assembled the JSON and cut spans containing thin/four-per-em spaces directly from the paper text; every span was then checked verbatim by script. Individuals: the case-report patient ('patient'); his father and mother, who were tested by Sanger sequencing and did not carry the variant (no variant rows, all checklist items not reported); and two previously published individuals described in the Discussion with individual-level detail: Iwasa's 33-year-old woman with HA20 ('ref (12) patient') and Zhang's neonatal-onset HA20 case ('ref (7) patient'). Not given rows: the patient's two half-brothers (described only as having 'no similar medical history', untested and unaffected); the girl in reference 6 (appears only in the reference-list title, not described in the text); group statements citing refs 1-14. The ref (7) variant row ('large deletion on chromosome 6q', gene not printed) comes from the reference-list title of ref 7 ('A20 haploinsufficiency in a neonate caused by a large deletion on chromosome 6q'); no variant row for ref (12) patient because the text prints no variant for her. Table 1 lab values were not converted to features unless the text calls them abnormal (CRP, WBC, ALT/AST, ANA, dsDNA-ELISA, MPO, PR3, GBM, IL-6, IL-10, TNF-alpha, IFN-gamma); the table note says bold marks abnormal results but the bold is lost in the Markdown, so out-of-range table-only values (e.g. low hemoglobin, low complement C3/C4, Coombs C3 and Coombs-Dott (++), anti-glycoprotein antibody 247.3, low albumin) are not recorded; '(-)' cells are undefined symbols and were not used as exclusions. Sputum culture Enterobacter cloacae (Table 1) recorded as observed. Genital ulcers set to excluded from 'No abnormalities were detected in the anus or external genitalia.' Gastrointestinal inflammation left not reported (diarrhoea only; gastroscopy/colonoscopy declined). Recurrent infections left not reported (COVID-19, one enterovirus episode and a sputum culture are reported, but the paper does not call infections recurrent). Hepatosplenomegaly not mapped to lymphoproliferation. Age at diagnosis is not stated as an age. Inconsistencies noticed (not about phenotypes): Table 1 gives creatinine with the same value and range as blood urea nitrogen (3.03 mmol/L, 0.8-5.3 mmol/L) and gives red blood cells the white-cell reference range; Figure 4 legend prints 'NM_001270508.2c.1876_1877del' without a colon and the abstract prints 'p. Leu626ValfsTer45' with a space; dsDNA-IIF is (-) while dsDNA-ELISA is positive (different assays).
